nodeNotes.capture-engine: Queues filtered rects during the walk, then scales, crops and uniformity-checks each one against the single screenshot.
nodeNotes.service-worker: Calls captureVisibleTab, which only extension contexts can do, and returns a reason instead of throwing on rate limits or restricted pages.
nodeNotes.tab-screenshot: A device-pixel PNG of the visible viewport only, so content scrolled out of view can never be recovered.

features.name: HTML and TOON export
features.summary: One shortcut opens your loot, previewed and ready to save.
features.description: Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+E opens a live preview at a few screen widths, plus the HTML and TOON source. TOON is a compact spec for LLMs, with embedded images cut down to a byte count so they don't eat the context.
features.underTheHood: Styles used more than once become shared classes, and one-offs stay inline. The payload waits in the worker's memory with a backup in session storage, since MV3 likes to kill the worker before the tab reads it. The preview iframe allows no scripts, so nothing captured can run.

steps.label: Cmd+Shift+E
steps.narration: The export key fires. If this frame has nothing selected, the worker rounds up selections from every frame.

steps.label: build request
steps.narration: Styles get deduplicated into shared tables, working on clones of the frozen trees. The live page isn't touched.

steps.label: the payload
steps.narration: The payload goes to the worker, with one retry if it was asleep. Failures say why and how big.

steps.label: export id
steps.narration: The worker fetches fonts, starts saving history without waiting on it, and opens the export tab.

steps.label: payload to writers
steps.narration: The tab builds the HTML and TOON in stages, painting in between so the progress bar isn't lying.

steps.label: HTML with inline fonts
steps.narration: The HTML goes into an iframe with scripts off. It resizes again at 120ms and 600ms for late fonts.

steps.label: rendered component
steps.narration: You see the component rebuilt from the export alone. Diagnostics explain anything dropped or turned into pixels.

algorithms.name: finalize() — from frozen trees to shared style tables
algorithms.summary: A multi-pass, DOM-free compiler from raw capture trees to class tables, inline overrides and hover selectors.
steps: Deep-clone each selection's raw tree (cloneNodeTree), so the frozen capture can be exported again later.
Count pass: walk every node and count styleKey(style). The key is the properties sorted by name and joined as "prop:value;".

Pass 0 (markHoverHosts): DFS with an ancestor stack. For each ancestor-hover rule recorded as `up` hops, mark stack[stack.length − up].needsClass so the ancestor gets a class to hang ".host:hover .child" on.

Pass 1 (assign): DFS. If a style key appears twice or more, or the node needs a class for a hover rule, give it a shared class sN (one per distinct key, via a Map). Otherwise move its style to node.inline. Pseudo before/after pairs are deduplicated by JSON key into pN classes.
Pass 2 (emitHovers): DFS with an ancestor stack. Emit ".sN:hover" for own hover differences and ".sHost:hover .sN" for ancestor rules, then merge rules with the same selector.

Group top-level selections by their real parent element. A group whose parent was flex or grid gets a wN wrapper carrying the parent's display, direction, wrap, justify, align, gap, grid templates and padding.

Renumber dropdown ids per selection so two captures can't both produce dd1, and pair each adopted menu with the selection it was adopted from (adoptedFrom), or failing that the nearest earlier non-adopted one.

normalizePosition(): a top-level absolute or fixed node gets inline position:relative with offsets and z-index reset, and a percentage translate removed. An adopted menu instead gets absolute at top:100%, left:0 under its trigger.
spliceRemoteFrames() last, once the parent's names are final.
algorithms.complexity: Linear in nodes: three DFS passes and one counting pass.

algorithms.name: buildPayload() — assembling the export
algorithms.summary: Merges per-selection results into one payload.
steps: Run finalize(selections).
Merge each selection's font registry: union the weight and italic sets and sum character counts.
pickFontFaces() → bundle list. buildFontPlan() → Google links, icon keys, primary font and whether it loads.
Merge remote frames' Google families (by family), icon keys and faces (by family|weight|style), skipping duplicates.
collectKeyframes(): split every animation-name in the style tables and inline styles on commas, and copy the @keyframes cssText for each name that is used.

Sum every numeric per-selection diagnostic, merge the icon-family counts, and return {url, title, viewport, pageBackground, styles, pseudos, wrappers, hovers, nodes, fonts, fontFaces, keyframes, diagnostics}.
algorithms.complexity: Linear in nodes and font entries.

algorithms.name: HtmlWriter.build() — payload to document
algorithms.summary: Renders the body first, then assembles CSS in a fixed cascade order.
steps: Head: charset, viewport, title, a preview-only <base target="_blank">, a "captured from" comment, one Google css2 <link> per family (ital,wght@ axes built from the weights and italics) and icon CDN links, with a preconnect when any link exists.
Body: when interactive, prepare dropdown pairs first, because that mutates tabindex and yields rules. Then call renderNode() for each top-level node.

renderNode(): a recursive pre-order walk. Text is escaped. A raw SVG gets class and style spliced into its root tag. A placeholder becomes a hatched div with a label. An gets its src. Void tags have no close tag. A single text child stays on one line. Otherwise children are indented one level deeper.

CSS order: :where() reset → placeholder CSS → interactive CSS and per-pair rules → surface background → optional backdrop surface → @font-face (data URIs in preview, fonts/… paths in the saved file) → @keyframes → .sN and .wN rules → hover rules → ::before/::after rules (content always emitted, even when empty).
cssString() escapes non-ASCII in content as \hex followed by a space, so private-use icon codepoints survive any encoding.
algorithms.complexity: Linear in nodes and rules.

algorithms.name: TOON serialization — ToonWriter.toToon()
algorithms.summary: A line-per-node, indentation-based text form of the payload.
steps: Sections are written in order: ## Meta, ## Styles, ## Wrappers, ## Hover Styles, ## Pseudo Styles, ## Structure.
Style bodies are written as "prop: value; prop: value", and any url(data:…) inside a value is truncated to its prefix plus "…(N bytes)".

writeNode() is a recursive pre-order walk with two spaces of indent per depth. A header is tag, then .classes, then [inline], then (attributes with booleans as bare flags, src/href data-URIs truncated, "icon" flag).
A single text child goes on the same line in quotes. Multiple children open "{", recurse, and close "}". Interleaved text becomes bare quoted lines, which keeps its position.
Raw SVG is collapsed onto one line. A placeholder is written as "@placeholder WxH \"label\"".
algorithms.complexity: Linear in nodes.

algorithms.name: Syntax highlighting — Highlight.highlight()
algorithms.summary: Escapes the source first, then highlights it in a single regex pass.
steps: Above 400KB, return the escaped text without highlighting.
Escape &, < and > first, so captured markup can never become live tags in the panel.
For HTML, split around the <style>…</style> island: HTML before and after, CSS inside.

Each mode runs one master alternation regex through String.replace with a callback that wraps exactly one token. The order of alternatives sets priority (comments, then strings, then tags or properties, then numbers). Because it is a single pass, text inside spans already emitted is never highlighted again.
algorithms.complexity: O(n), one regex pass per section.

algorithms.name: Preview sizing — fitFrame()
algorithms.summary: Sizes the sandboxed iframe to its content, and scales fixed widths down to fit the pane.
steps: available = pane width − 44px. target = available for Fit, otherwise 1280, 768 or 375.
Collapse the iframe to height 0, then read max(documentElement.scrollHeight, body.scrollHeight, 40). allow-same-origin is what allows this read.
scale = available ÷ target if the target is wider than the pane. Apply transform: scale() to the stage and set its height to height × scale.
Run again on load, then at 120ms and 600ms for webfont swaps, and on resize.
algorithms.complexity: O(1) per call.

export.js — boot(), renderPayload(), renderDiagnostics(), renderPreview(), fitFrame()
lib/highlight.js — escape-first, single-pass highlighter, 400 KB limit

deep.algorithm: Two-phase capture, style-table compiler, shared writers
deep.idea: Freeze the DOM at click time, compile it into deduplicated style tables at export, and render HTML and TOON from that single payload.
how: Click: smartExpand picks the element; captureRaw walks it into a frozen tree of plain objects, with styles already pruned.
Export: finalize clones the trees, keys each style set, mints .sN/.pN/.wN, and writes hover selectors.
buildPayload adds the font plan, referenced @keyframes and diagnostics; one runtime message carries everything to the worker.
The worker fetches fonts, stores the payload in a Map plus a session mirror, records history, and opens export.html?id.
The tab runs HtmlWriter.build twice (relative fonts for saving, inline for the preview) and ToonWriter.toToon once.
Saving downloads a Blob, polls downloads.search for the absolute path, and copies that path to the clipboard.
deep.example:
li A, li B: {padding-top:8px; color:#fff}; li C also has a background (illustrative) → A, B get class s1; C keeps style="…" inline (one-off) A, B, C selected separately; parent ul is display:flex; gap:12px →
A B C
with .w1 { display: flex; gap: 12px }
deep.why: Reading the DOM at export time would capture whatever the page shows later, like a rotated carousel. Sharing the writer files with the Node CLI keeps both outputs identical by construction, apart from what TOON strips (images, bundled fonts, keyframes).
deep.cost: finalize is linear: one counting pass plus three depth-first passes.

stepNotes.2: styleKey: properties sorted and joined 'prop:value;'. Keys used twice or more, or needing a hover class, become sN in depth-first order; others stay inline. Flex/grid sibling selections wrap in wN. normalizePosition makes absolute roots position:relative.
stepNotes.3: chrome.storage.local caps at 10MB without unlimitedStorage, and full pages with bitmaps exceed that. The in-memory Map is fast; the session mirror (only under 4MB) survives MV3 killing the idle worker before the tab reads it.
stepNotes.5: HTML: links, then :where() reset, placeholder, dropdown, surface, @font-face, @keyframes, .sN/.wN, hover, pseudo. Zero specificity lets .sN win without !important. TOON: '## Styles' then '.s1: display: flex'; base64 becomes '…(2048 bytes)', counting base64 characters.
stepNotes.6: No allow-scripts, so captured code can't run; allow-same-origin lets fitFrame collapse the height to 0, read scrollHeight, apply it, and scale fixed widths to the pane. It re-fits at 120ms and 600ms for webfont swaps.

nodes.details: Shows live status and recent captures, and lets you rebind all seven shortcuts. On chrome:// pages it explains that Chrome blocks extensions there instead of showing dead buttons.
keyFiles: popup.js — boot(), renderStatus(), renderHistory(), isBlocked(), shortcut editor
nodes.interesting: Opening the popup is the start button, so most of the time you never click anything inside it.

nodes.label: Target Page
nodes.details: DOM Heist mostly just reads it. Its writes are small: closed menus and <details> open for a few milliseconds, a crosshair cursor style, a hidden probe iframe and a tiny helper stylesheet inside shadow roots.
keyFiles: test/fixtures.html — every capture path on one page
nodes.interesting: It only borrows what it has to: closed menus and <details> open for a few milliseconds, then go back in a finally block. A polite burglar who still leaves a sticky note in your shadow roots.

nodes.label: Selection Overlay
nodes.summary: The outline you see, and the input layer underneath.
nodes.details: Lives in a closed shadow root at z-index 2147483647, with pointer events off. Subtle. It catches clicks, wheel and keys before the page sees them, and handles the shortcuts.
keyFiles: contentScript.js — buildUI(), onPointerMove(), onPointerDown(), onKeyDown(), setPaused(), message handling section
nodes.interesting: The mode toolbar dodges your cursor. Get within 32px and it hops to the other side of the screen.

nodes.label: Capture Engine
nodes.summary: Freezes your pick, then packs it for export.
nodes.details: Phase one runs when you click and reads everything, 180 properties per node plus fonts, images and frames. Phase two runs at export on clones, never changing the page (it only peeks at font links and the background), and builds shared style tables.
keyFiles: contentScript.js — captureRaw(), walkElement(), buildMatchIndex(), finalize(), buildPayload()
nodes.interesting: Two phases is why a carousel freezes where it was when you clicked, and why you can export the same pick twice.

nodes.label: Defaults Probe
nodes.summary: A hidden iframe that knows every tag's default look.
nodes.details: It loads the export's own CSS reset and builds each tag in the right parent, like a td inside a table. Matching captured values get dropped. If CSP blocks it, a fallback table steps in.
keyFiles: lib/reset.js — note on why the reset is the pruning baseline
nodes.interesting: Change the reset and the pruning moves with it, so the export can't drift from what was pruned.

nodes.label: Frame Instance
tech: Content script in a cross-origin iframe
nodes.summary: DOM Heist's own copy inside someone else's iframe.
nodes.details: The content script runs in every frame, so one of these sits inside each cross-origin iframe. When asked, it captures its own page and reports things the parent can't see, like whether it scrolls and its background colour.
nodes.interesting: A frame capturing for its parent never starts handshakes of its own, so a page that frames itself can't recurse forever.

nodes.label: Service Worker
nodes.summary: The switchboard that talks to every frame.
nodes.details: Broadcasts commands to every frame and merges their replies. It also fetches fonts, takes the one screenshot, and sets the toolbar badge: amber while selecting, blue while interacting.
keyFiles: background.js — message router, runExport(), broadcast(), mergePayloads(), captureRemoteFrame(), captureTab(), fetchFontBinary(), history section
nodes.interesting: Only the worker can turn a token into a frame id, because Chrome tells it who sent the message. That's what makes spoofing impossible.

nodes.label: History IndexedDB
nodes.details: IndexedDB with two stores: small summary rows and the big payload blobs. After every save it trims down to the newest 10 and 60 MB in total.
keyFiles: background.js — HISTORY_DB, HISTORY_LIMIT, HISTORY_BYTE_BUDGET, openHistoryDb(), pruneHistory()
nodes.interesting: Keeping summaries apart from payloads means the history list loads without unpacking megabytes of JSON.

nodes.label: Session Mirror
nodes.summary: A spare copy in case the worker dies.
nodes.details: Payloads under 4 MB get copied here. If MV3 kills the worker between opening the export tab and the tab reading it, this copy saves the day.

nodes.label: Shortcut Store
nodes.summary: Your seven key bindings, synced by Chrome.
nodes.details: One key holding all seven bindings. The popup writes it, every content script reads it, and Cmd/Ctrl+Shift defaults fill in if it's empty. Matching happens on keydown, not through Chrome's commands API.

nodes.label: Tab Screenshot
nodes.summary: A PNG of whatever is on screen.
nodes.details: Called at most once per capture. The API is rate-limited, needs the tab active and visible, and only sees the viewport.

nodes.label: Downloads API
nodes.summary: Saves your files and reports where they landed.
nodes.details: The export tab hands Chrome a Blob URL, then keeps polling until the download completes, because only then does the real file path exist.
nodes.interesting: Polling is the only way to learn the real path on disk, and the paste-into-an-LLM workflow needs exactly that.

nodes.label: Export Tab
nodes.details: Takes the payload and builds the preview, HTML, TOON and diagnostics in stages. It also handles the toggles, saving, the fonts ZIP and history. It never looks at the captured page.
keyFiles: export.js — boot(), renderPayload(), renderDiagnostics(), fitFrame(), saveFonts(), openHistoryEntry()
export.html — layout and sandboxed preview iframe
nodes.interesting: Opening an old capture from history runs the same code as a fresh export.

nodes.label: HTML/TOON Writers
nodes.summary: Pure functions that turn a payload into HTML or TOON.
nodes.details: html-writer builds the reset, fonts, keyframes, CSS rules and the node tree. toon-writer converts to and from TOON. The same files run in the extension and in Node.
nodes.interesting: The CLI loads these same files, so it rebuilds the same HTML from a .toon. The only gaps are what TOON leaves out: embedded images, bundled fonts and @keyframes.

nodes.label: Sandboxed Preview
nodes.summary: Shows the export with real fonts and no scripts.
nodes.details: An iframe sandboxed without allow-scripts, so nothing lifted from a stranger's website can run. Same-origin is allowed so the tab can measure its height.
nodes.interesting: No scripts is why dropdowns open with pure CSS. A test checks it with a canary script that must never run.

nodes.label: Font Hosts
nodes.summary: Wherever the page's self-hosted fonts already live.
nodes.details: The only servers the extension itself talks to. The worker fetches each font file with no cookies and a 10s timeout.

nodes.label: Font/Icon CDNs
nodes.summary: Public CDNs the exported HTML links to.
nodes.details: Requested by the exported page itself, never by the extension. Google fonts plus icon sets like Font Awesome and Material Icons.
nodes.interesting: One link per Google family on purpose. Ask for several at once and one unknown family gets the whole request a 400.

edges.label: opens popup
edges.payload: Toolbar icon click
edges.details: Opening the popup starts selection. Restricted pages get an explanation instead.

edges.label: hover, click, keys
edges.payload: pointermove, pointerdown, wheel, keydown
edges.details: In Select mode clicks get swallowed. In Interact mode only movement and shortcuts are watched.

edges.label: interacts with page
edges.payload: Hover and clicks while in Interact mode
edges.details: To open menus or hover panels before grabbing them.

edges.label: save, copy, toggle
edges.payload: Button clicks
edges.details: Preview width, Interactive mode, copy, save and history.

edges.label: CMD + HISTORY_*
edges.payload: { type: 'DOMHEIST_CMD', cmd: 'start'|'clear'|'export', tabId }; DOMHEIST_HISTORY_LIST / OPEN_HISTORY / HISTORY_DELETE
edges.details: Commands and history requests. The popup closes itself after a successful export.

edges.label: STATUS/PAUSE/SHORTCUTS
edges.payload: DOMHEIST_STATUS → { active, paused, count, isFrame }; DOMHEIST_PAUSE; DOMHEIST_SHORTCUTS
edges.details: Polled every 700ms. No reply means the script isn't loaded, so it suggests a reload.

edges.label: saves bindings
edges.payload: { shortcuts: { start|export|fullpage|history|pause|grab|diagnose: { primary, shift, alt, key } } }
edges.details: Checked so every action has a key, then merged onto the defaults.

edges.label: loadShortcuts()
edges.payload: get({ shortcuts: null })
edges.details: Falls back to the default shortcuts if nothing is saved or the read fails.

edges.label: addSelection / export
edges.payload: addSelection(el, replace, { noAdopt }); grabHovered(exact); requestExport() → buildPayload()
edges.details: One capture at a time. Exporting mid-walk gets a 'Still extracting' message.

edges.label: raw tree, progress
edges.payload: { node, diag, registry, parent, rect, position }; onProgress(fraction)
edges.details: Progress updates at most once every 16ms.

edges.label: reads DOM + styles
edges.payload: getComputedStyle, cssRules, querySelectorAll per rule, getBoundingClientRect, toDataURL, currentSrc
edges.details: Stylesheets read once per capture. Closed menus are revealed, then put back.

edges.label: layer appeared
edges.payload: childList and attribute records (style, class, hidden, aria-hidden, data-state, open, popover)
edges.details: Only during selection mode, capped at 240 tracked layers.

edges.label: defaultsFor(tag)
edges.payload: tag → default computed values under RESET_CSS
edges.details: Cached per tag, with a fallback table if CSP blocks the iframe.

edges.label: posts token
edges.payload: { __domheist: 'domheist-frame-hello', token }
edges.details: Sent to any origin, since the frame's is unknown. The token carries no data.

edges.label: FRAME_HELLO token
edges.payload: { type: 'DOMHEIST_FRAME_HELLO', token }
edges.details: The worker notes which frame sent it and forgets after 30 seconds.

edges.label: EXPORT/REMOTE/TAB
edges.payload: DOMHEIST_EXPORT { payload }; DOMHEIST_CAPTURE_REMOTE { token, timeout: 4000 }; DOMHEIST_CAPTURE_TAB
edges.details: One retry after 150ms if the worker was asleep. Gives up at 30s.

edges.label: grab/badge/history
edges.payload: DOMHEIST_CMD { cmd: 'grab', exact }; DOMHEIST_ACTIVE { active, paused }; DOMHEIST_OPEN_HISTORY
edges.details: Sets the badge: amber while selecting, blue while interacting. Cleared on navigation.

edges.label: broadcast to frames
edges.payload: DOMHEIST_START | CLEAR | GRAB | TOAST
edges.details: Every frame, 4s timeout each. Frames without the script get skipped.

edges.label: COLLECT, replies
edges.payload: DOMHEIST_COLLECT → payload|null; replies to CAPTURE_REMOTE and CAPTURE_TAB
edges.details: Frames mid-capture reply null. Multiple payloads get merged into one.

edges.label: CAPTURE_FRAME
edges.payload: → { ok, payload, url }
edges.details: Only after the token is claimed. Each token works exactly once.

edges.label: captureVisibleTab
edges.payload: { format: 'png' } → data URL
edges.details: At most once per capture. Errors come back as a reason.

edges.label: GET font binaries
edges.payload: @font-face URL → bytes → { url, path, ok, base64, mime }
edges.details: No cookies, 10s timeout, all in parallel so one failure doesn't sink the rest.

edges.label: put/get/prune
edges.payload: meta rows and blob payloads
edges.details: Not awaited, so a history hiccup never breaks an export. Keeps 10 entries.

edges.label: mirrors payload
edges.payload: { 'payload:<exportId>': JSON }
edges.details: Only under 4 MB. Read only if the in-memory copy got lost.

edges.label: opens export tab
edges.payload: export.html?id=<cx…> | export.html?history=<id|list>
edges.details: If the tab can't open, the payload is dropped and the reason returned.

edges.label: payload, history, fonts
edges.payload: DOMHEIST_GET_PAYLOAD / RELEASE_PAYLOAD; HISTORY_LIST / GET / DELETE; FETCH_FONT { url, path, mime }
edges.details: Each failed font gets one retry before zipping. Expired payloads ask you to re-run.

edges.label: build() + toToon()
edges.payload: HtmlWriter.build(payload, opts) → HTML; ToonWriter.toToon(payload) → TOON
edges.details: Saved HTML gets relative font paths, the preview gets inline fonts.

edges.label: srcdoc
edges.payload: Full HTML document with inline fonts and <base target="_blank">
edges.details: Sized to fit on load, then rechecked at 120ms and 600ms.

edges.label: loads stylesheets
edges.payload: fonts.googleapis.com css2 per family; icon CSS on cdnjs/jsDelivr
edges.details: The saved preview.html makes the same requests when opened later.

edges.label: downloads.download
edges.payload: { url: blob:…, filename: preview.html | component.toon | preview-fonts.zip, saveAs: false }
edges.details: Polls every 120ms for up to 8s, then copies the file path.
